item.text: I’ll trace the existing comment schemas, repository patterns, and issue read authorization/member lookup, then add the three exports using those conventions.

item.command: /bin/zsh -lc "sed -n '1,300p' src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts && sed -n '1,260p' src/server/repositories/member-repository.ts && sed -n '1,240p' src/server/services/_support.ts && sed -n '1,220p' src/lib/tenant.ts && sed -n '1,260p' src/lib/permissions.ts && rg -n \"list.*Author|active member|listMembers|comment:read|TenantScope|NotFound|PermissionDenied|Permission\" src"

/bin/zsh -lc "sed -n '1,300p' src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts && sed -n '1,260p' src/server/repositories/member-repository.ts && sed -n '1,240p' src/server/services/_support.ts && sed -n '1,220p' src/lib/tenant.ts && sed -n '1,260p' src/lib/permissions.ts && rg -n \"list.*Author|active member|listMembers|comment:read|TenantScope|NotFound|PermissionDenied|Permission\" src"

item.text: The service can reuse the existing thread permission check and scoped issue lookup. I’ll gather unique issue/comment author and assignee ids, then keep only users whose membership is present and has `active` status.
